page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and driven by custom Intel Xeon 8488C processors operating at a nominal 3.2 GHz. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine provides 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU allocation is burstable, making it suitable for varying compute loads. Memory configuration includes 32.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM clocked at 5 GHz, maintaining a compute-tailored 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no bundled local storage and features a baseline network throughput of 3 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show strong results in single-threaded operations and lightweight model execution. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a top-tier single-core score of 2203.0 along with elevated text processing performance. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 33.24 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile of tested instances. For lightweight artificial intelligence tasks, the instance achieved 289.46 tokens per second during text generation using a 135M parameter model. Broader multi-core and system throughput metrics, such as a PassMark CPU score of 24806.62, a Geekbench multi-core score of 13421.0, and 20.47 million Redis SET operations per second, consistently place within the middle 50% category across the fleet.

Hardware capabilities include advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16, along with Intel AMX tile and int8 execution for matrix operations. These vector extensions provide acceleration for compute-heavy routines and cryptography tasks without dedicated accelerator cards. The trade-off lies in the burstable CPU allocation and the absence of local ephemeral storage, which requires relying entirely on network-attached EBS volumes for data persistence. This profile delivers competitive compute efficiency for workloads that encounter baseline processing with intermittent utilization spikes.

Workloads well aligned with the c7i-flex.4xlarge include web serving, CI/CD application build pipelines, batch processing, small-to-medium language model inference, and microservices architectures requiring modern DDR5 memory bandwidth and solid single-thread performance without continuous maximum CPU utilization.
